title: apps/advisor control flow: admission-triggered checks, scheduler, registry
answers: How does a Check actually get run in apps/advisor?
What triggers a check run / retry in the advisor app?
Where is the advisor check scheduler and how does MT vs ST work?
How does the frontend plugin talk to apps/advisor?
body:
apps/advisor is its own Go module (apps/advisor/go.mod, no TS codegen: kinds/manifest.cue codegen.ts.enabled=false) with no frontend in this repo — the external `grafana-advisor-app` plugin renders results, reached from public/app only via usePluginFunctions extension points (public/app/features/connections/hooks/useDatasourceAdvisorChecks.tsx).
Control flow for running a check: `app.go:New` registers an admission Validator on the `Check` kind; AdmissionActionCreate spawns `utils.go:processCheck`, a retry-annotation update spawns `utils.go:processCheckRetry` — there is no RPC to "run a check", you create/patch a `Check` object and the webhook does the work async.
Two background Runnables drive creation: `checktyperegisterer.Runner.Run` (checktyperegisterer.go) upserts one CheckType per registered check per namespace on boot; `checkscheduler.Runner.Run` (checkscheduler.go) picks `runST` or `runMT` (mtcheckscheduler.go, cluster-wide namespace discovery + fan-out capped at maxConcurrency=10) via `isMT()`, and on a timer creates a fresh `Check` per type, which fires the admission webhook above.
Both Runnables iterate `checkregistry.Service.Checks()` (checkregistry.go) — this is the single DI seam/source of truth for "what checks exist".
Wired into the server via pkg/registry/apps/advisor/register.go:ProvideAppInstaller → apps/advisor/pkg/app/app.go:ProvideAppInstaller → pkg/server/wireext/oss.go.
Custom app routes: POST .../register → checktyperegisterer; GET .../translations → translations.Get (serves embedded i18n JSON to the plugin).
